number.why: The abstract supports 6 versus 9 in-hospital deaths and randomized denominators of 61 versus 59, yielding a reconstructed RR of approximately 0.64481. It does not explicitly bind those denominators to the served intention-to-treat population. The ruling overlooks a held report explicitly tabulating intention-to-treat mortality: the same death totals, but denominators of 60 versus 59. Thus, unconditional confirmation of the served population-specific number is unwarranted, and the claim that no held source identifies a mortality analysis population is incorrect. The packet does not resolve whether the later report's smaller population should replace the original randomized denominator. The published 95% CI describes an absolute difference, not an RR.

quotes.span: Patients were randomized to receive either an intravenous bolus of 0.5 mg/kg per 12 hours of methylprednisolone (n = 61) or placebo (n = 59) for 5 days started within 36 hours of hospital admission.

In-hospital mortality did not differ between the 2 groups (6 patients [10%] in the methylprednisolone group vs 9 patients [15%] in the placebo group; P = .37); the difference between groups was 5% (95% CI, -6% to 17%).

entry.why: Adult hospitalized patients with severe community-acquired pneumonia and high inflammation are an eligible subset of the question's population. Intravenous methylprednisolone versus placebo, alongside antibiotic care, establishes the relevant treatment comparison. Restricted severity and inflammation criteria limit generalizability without undermining entry eligibility.

Patients were randomized to receive either an intravenous bolus of 0.5 mg/kg per 12 hours of methylprednisolone (n = 61) or placebo (n = 59) for 5 days started within 36 hours of hospital admission.
All patients were treated with antibiotics according to current international guidelines[ ].

missed: The explicitly labeled intention-to-treat mortality table creates an unresolved denominator discrepancy: 44 + 16 methylprednisolone recipients versus 61 randomized in the abstract. Using that table gives a reconstructed RR of (6/60)/(9/59) = approximately 0.65556, rather than 0.64481. These are derived alternatives, not published RRs; the table does not by itself justify substituting its denominator for the original report's.
